newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices open season on firm note.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices open season on firm note.

text.p: Australian wool prices began the 1997/98 season on a firm note in Sydney and Fremantle this week, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said on Friday,
"With the positive sentiment evident within the wool trade over the break, the market opened with strength," Wesfarmers said.
The eastern market indicator rose two cents to end the week at 718 cents a kg clean from the 1996/97 close on July 4 while western indicator lost one cent to 664 cents a kg clean.
The eastern indicator stood well above the year earlier level of 593 cents a kg, Wool International (WI) figures show.

The Australian Council of Wool Exporters said that although some people might have been expecting more significant upward movement in prices, exporters consider the market performed solidly under prevailing circumstances.
A total of 79,021 bales were offered with a pass in rate of 10.3 percent.
WI said it sold 11,696 bales in the week ended July 31, leaving its stockpile of unsold wool at 1,522,168 bales.
In the futures market, a total of 26 lots were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended July 31 and open interest increased by 21 contracts to close at 1,297.
The near August contract closed 33 cents down at 871 cents a kg clean.
Sales next week are in Sydney and Melbourne with 92,000 bales rostered for sale.
